questions.text: Let $\{a_n\}$ satisfy $a_1 = 1$ and $\frac{1}{a_n} + \frac{2}{a_{n+1}} = 0$ for $n \ge 1$. Sequence $\{b_n\}$ satisfies $b_n = |a_n|$. Find the sum of the first $n$ terms $S_n$ of sequence $\{b_n\}$.
questions.explanation:
From $\frac{1}{a_n} + \frac{2}{a_{n+1}} = 0$, we have $\frac{2}{a_{n+1}} = -\frac{1}{a_n} \implies a_{n+1} = -2a_n$.
This is a geometric progression with $a_1 = 1$ and common ratio $q = -2$.
Thus $a_n = (-2)^{n-1}$.
Then $b_n = |a_n| = |(-2)^{n-1}| = 2^{n-1}$, which is a geometric progression with first term $1$ and common ratio $2$.
$$S_n = \frac{1(2^n - 1)}{2 - 1} = 2^n - 1$$

questions.text:
In a survey on running app preferences, $200$ high school students and $80$ university students were sampled:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline \textbf{Group} & \textbf{App A} & \textbf{App B} & \textbf{App C} & \textbf{App D} \\ \hline \text{High School} & 80 & 40 & 60 & 20 \\ \hline \text{University} & 30 & 20 & 20 & 10 \\ \hline \end{array}$$
Assuming preferences between the two groups are independent, if one person is randomly selected from each group, what is the probability that their favorite running apps are DIFFERENT?
questions.explanation:
Use the complementary probability: $P(\text{different}) = 1 - P(\text{same})$.
High school distribution: $P(A) = \frac{80}{200} = \frac{2}{5}$, $P(B) = \frac{40}{200} = \frac{1}{5}$, $P(C) = \frac{60}{200} = \frac{3}{10}$, $P(D) = \frac{20}{200} = \frac{1}{10}$.
University distribution: $P(A) = \frac{30}{80} = \frac{3}{8}$, $P(B) = \frac{20}{80} = \frac{1}{4}$, $P(C) = \frac{20}{80} = \frac{1}{4}$, $P(D) = \frac{10}{80} = \frac{1}{8}$.
Probability of both picking the same app:
$$P(\text{same}) = \left(\frac{2}{5}\times\frac{3}{8}\right) + \left(\frac{1}{5}\times\frac{1}{4}\right) + \left(\frac{3}{10}\times\frac{1}{4}\right) + \left(\frac{1}{10}\times\frac{1}{8}\right)$$
$$= \frac{6}{40} + \frac{2}{40} + \frac{3}{40} + \frac{1}{80} = \frac{11}{40} + \frac{1}{80} = \frac{23}{80}$$
$$P(\text{different}) = 1 - \frac{23}{80} = \frac{57}{80}$$
